latest_release.name: v0.0.16
latest_release.body:
**fx uses 41% fewer tokens. The CLI is 2.8% smaller. libfx npm downloads are about 60% smaller. Edit files up to 4× larger, now up to 16 MiB.**

### Improvements

- Long agent turns use less CPU. A paired local benchmark with 1,000 tool steps used 50–59% less CPU than the previous implementation.
- `fx update` now works as an alias for `fx upgrade`, including `--channel` and `--json`.
- Tool results keep their original timestamps when a turn is rebuilt or resumed.
- The macOS arm64 CLI binary is 2.8% smaller (5.97 MiB vs 6.15 MiB), saving 180,576 bytes.
- Installing libfx downloads about 60% less than 0.0.15, including the matching native platform package. On Apple Silicon, the download drops from 19.08 MB to 7.32 MB, a 61.6% reduction.
- Across macOS and Linux builds, total libfx npm downloads are 60.1–61.6% smaller. Unpacked package contents shrink from 43.55 MB to roughly 18–19.4 MB.
- libfx installs the native addon for your platform instead of carrying every platform’s binary. By default, Node.js loads the WebAssembly backend only when native execution is unavailable.
- Across ten model families, caching scenarios used 41% fewer uncached input tokens than 0.0.15. Requests that broke the cached prompt prefix fell from 80 to 10, an 87.5% reduction.
- Uncached input tokens fell 79% on Claude Sonnet 5.5, 78% on Claude Haiku 5.5, and 76% on GPT-6.1 in that comparison. Results varied by model, with MiniMax using 3% more.
- Prompt caching on supported models now reuses shared instructions across workspaces and worktrees.
- Changing branches or permissions, reading new folder rules, and resuming a conversation keep the earlier conversation available for prompt caching.
- Named skills send their full instructions with the turn that invokes them instead of adding them to every later request.
- Browser apps can bundle only the WebAssembly module they use instead of both the agent and terminal modules.
- The libfx WebAssembly core is 12.8% smaller than in 0.0.15 (2.16 MiB vs 2.47 MiB), and the terminal is 20.1% smaller (3.39 MiB vs 4.24 MiB). These are uncompressed binary sizes.
- `edit_file` and `write_file` handle files up to 16 MiB, up from 4 MiB.
- File edits save their diffs instead of full copies of the file before and after every change. The diff remains available in Ctrl+O after resume, with an omitted-row notice if it exceeds the saved-text limit.
- `/model` finds models from abbreviated or slightly mistyped provider and model names.
- Saved sessions retain token usage from each model reply, including replies received before an interrupted turn, and continue counting after resume.
- Subagent token usage is saved in each subagent’s own session and remains separate from its parent’s total.
- `fx ask --json` includes cached-read and cache-write token counts when the provider reports them.
- Global `~/.fx/AGENTS.md` can link to an instruction file elsewhere inside your home directory.
- Slack sign-in requests the permissions needed to search private channels and direct messages you can access.

### Bug Fixes

- When repeated response failures stop a turn, fx keeps its prompt, partial reply, and completed tool calls. The next prompt can continue from that work, including after resuming the session.
- Retrying a cancelled libfx prompt with the same turn ID returns the ended turn instead of running the prompt and its tools again.
- Opening an edit in Ctrl+O no longer crashes when the file contains terminal escape sequences.
- Editing files containing invalid UTF-8 no longer prevents the session from saving or stops the turn. Invalid bytes appear as readable escapes in previews and saved diffs.
- Fixed `fx balance` startup when reading a saved credential from the system key store.
- Stopping a terminal also stops commands running in nested shells and separate job-control groups instead of leaving them running.
- MCP server failures retain their final error output, including when the server exits immediately.
- `/usage` in the brows

It's one native binary written in Zig, so there is no runtime to install, and it runs the same on your laptop, in CI, or inside an agent sandbox. Its output is closer to a Unix shell than an IDE, because the conversation prints into your terminal's scrollback instead of filling the screen. fx is meant to be embedded and extended. Scripts call it with `fx ask`, editors connect over the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), and JavaScript apps run the same agent core through [libfx](sdk/README.md) with their own tools. Skills, MCP servers, and your project's `AGENTS.md` add to what the agent knows and can do.

## Features - **Small and fast**: CI fails a pull request if any benchmarked command, such as `fx help` or `fx status --json`, takes longer than 2 ms on Linux ([benchmarks](benchmarks/)). Stable releases for Apple silicon must also fit under a fixed size limit. - **Built-in tools**: fx finds, reads, and edits files, runs shell commands, searches the web and reads URLs, and delegates work to subagents. A development server or file watcher can keep running while it works ([tools](https://fx.sh/docs/capabilities/tools)). - **Model choice**: sign in to Vercel AI Gateway, use a ChatGPT or Grok subscription, or connect an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint such as Ollama or OpenRouter ([custom model connections](https://fx.sh/docs/configure-fx/custom-model-connections)). - **Inline output**: you can scroll, search, and copy the conversation like any other command's output, and tmux bindings and copy mode keep working. Terminals that support the [Program Status Protocol](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status) can also show when fx is busy or waiting for you. - **Your own shell**: commands run in your login shell, with your aliases, functions, and `PATH`. fx runs your startup files once and reuses the result until one of them changes, so a slow `.zshrc` doesn't slow down every command. Commands also receive `AI_AGENT=fx` in their environment, so development tools can detect fx. - **Permissions**: the default `auto` mode runs routine work, such as editing project files and running tests, without asking. Anything else goes first to a model that checks the exact action for prompt injection or malicious behavior, and fx holds the action if the check finds a problem. Switch to `ask` to approve each action yourself, or to `full-access` to turn the checks off ([permissions](https://fx.sh/docs/configure-fx/permissions)). - **Sessions**: fx saves your conversations under `~/.fx/sessions/`, and `fx -c` picks up where you left off in a project. When a conversation fills the model's context, fx compacts older turns but keeps their full text on disk, where the agent can look it up ([sessions](https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/sessions)). ## Install ```bash curl -fsSL https://fx.sh/setup.sh | bash ``` fx runs on macOS and Linux, on x86_64 and arm64. The installer puts it in `~/.local/bin`. fx checks for updates in the background, and `fx upgrade` installs the latest release right away. [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) lists what changed in each release. You can also [try fx in your browser](https://fx.sh/try) without installing anything. ## Quick start Sign in with one of these: ```bash fx login # Vercel AI Gateway fx login codex # ChatGPT subscription fx login grok # Grok subscription fx login vercel --api-key # AI Gateway API key ``` Then open a project and start fx: ```bash cd your-project fx ``` Type what you want done and press Enter. `/help` lists the slash commands. If something doesn't work, run `fx doctor` to check your setup. To send one request without the interactive shell, use `fx ask`. Add `--json` when a script needs to read the result: ```bash fx ask "explain the changes in this repository" fx ask --json "summarize the failing tests" | jq -r .final_output ``` ## Embed and extend | Surface | Use it for | | --- | --- | | fx ask | One request from a script or CI job. `--json` returns structured output, and `--resume` continues a saved session. | | fx acp | Editors and other [Agent Client Protocol](https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/acp) clients, over stdio. | | [libfx](https://www.npmjs.com/package/libfx) | The agent core as a JavaScript library, built as a native Node.js addon and as WebAssembly. `createFxAgent()` runs an agent with your own tools, MCP clients, and skills, and `createFxTerminal()` embeds the fx terminal. | The [libfx README](sdk/README.md) and the [libfx docs](https://fx.sh/docs/lib) cover the API. The WebAssembly build is experimental. The CLI also picks up these extensions: - **Skills**: fx loads skills from `.fx/skills` and `~/.fx/skills`, and from the folders other agents use, such as `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`. The model sees each skill's name and description and reads the full instructions only when it needs them, so installed skills take little room in the context ([skills](https://fx.sh/docs/capabilities/skills)). - **MCP servers**: `/mcp add slack` sets up Slack, and `fx mcp` manages servers from your terminal. A server's tool schemas load when the model looks for them ([MCP](https://fx.sh/docs/capabilities/mcp)). - **Project instructions**: fx follows the `AGENTS.md` in your project, nested `AGENTS.md` files for the directories they cover, and `~/.fx/AGENTS.md` for your own instructions across projects ([project instructions](https://fx.sh/docs/configure-fx/project-instructions)). ## Examples [`examples/`](examples) has small libfx apps you can run with an AI Gateway API key: - [`node-chat`](examples/node-chat): a terminal chat with streamed replies. - [`browser-agent`](examples/browser-agent): the agent in WebAssembly behind a plain HTML form. - [`nextjs-agent`](examples/nextjs-agent): a Next.js App Router form with a streaming route handler. - [`nuxt-agent`](examples/nuxt-agent): the same idea in Nuxt, with a Nitro route. ## Documentation The manual at [fx.sh/docs](https://fx.sh/docs) covers models, permissions, configuration, skills, MCP, sessions, and every CLI and slash command. ## For coding agents To learn fx, read the manual as Markdown. [fx.sh/llms.txt](https://fx.sh/llms.txt) indexes every page, [fx.sh/llms-full.txt](https://fx.sh/llms-full.txt) puts the whole manual in one file, and adding `.md` to any docs URL returns that page as Markdown. For the flags of the installed version, run `fx --help`. To run fx from your own tools, use `fx ask`. It takes the prompt as arguments or on stdin, writes its result to stdout and progress and diagnostics to stderr, and exits with a nonzero status when the request fails. With `--json`, the final answer is in `final_output`. To inspect a user's setup, run `fx status --json` for configuration and runtime information, or `fx doctor --json` for local health checks. Neither changes the setup. `fx ask` uses the user's saved permission mode, which is `auto` unless they changed it. Pass `--full-access` only when the user asks for it, because it turns off fx's permission checks. To change fx itself, read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) first, then build and verify the change as described in [Contributing](#contributing). ## Feedback Run `/feedback` inside fx to open the feedback form, or [open an issue](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/issues/new/choose). If something looks wrong in your terminal, `/trace` creates a private diagnostic report you can attach ([share feedback](https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/share-feedback)). ## Contributing You need [Zig 0.17.0](https://ziglang.org/download/) to build fx: ```bash git clone https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx.git cd fx zig build ./zig-out/bin/fx ``` Test your changes with the freshly built `./zig-out/bin/fx`, because a bare `fx` may be an older copy on your `PATH`. `zig build test` runs the unit tests, which sit next to the code they cover. The end-to-end tests in [`tests/e2e/`](tests/e2e) drive the built binary through tmux and need [Bun](https://bun.sh). The source is laid out like this: ```text fx/ ├── src/ │ ├── main.zig entry point that wires everything together │ ├── core/ agent loop, sessions, config, permissions, MCP, skills │ ├── builtins/ built-in tool specs, providers, and the system prompt │ ├── tools/ built-in tools: files, shell, web, skills, subagents │ ├── ui/ terminal rendering and input │ ├── gateway/ model provider transport │ ├── mcp/ MCP engine │ └── acp/ Agent Client Protocol server ├── sdk/ libfx, the JavaScript library ├── tests/ end-to-end tests and model evals └── benchmarks/ startup, memory, and latency benchmarks ``` Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before you open a pull request. It covers verification, CI, and PR labels. If a coding agent is helping you, point it at [For coding agents](#for-coding-agents). ## Security Report vulnerabilities through the [contact page](https://fx.sh/contact) instead of a public issue. ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE). Third-party licenses and attributions are in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). ## Credits Interface sounds by [cuelume](https://github.com/Danilaa1/cuelume).
